narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. At 6-10 years, you fall into a mid-career range where many employees begin exploring new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay who have only 1-5 years of overall experience.

Closely related, the time you have spent in your current organization (1-5 years) is the second most influential factor. This relatively short tenure in your present role also signals to the model a higher likelihood of departure compared with longer-serving colleagues who tend to remain.

The third important element works in the opposite direction: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities actually pulls the prediction slightly toward staying. However, it was not strong enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to increase your sense of stability and growth potential here. You may want to reflect on whether your current path aligns with your longer-term ambitions. (218 words)
